  - DESTROY_OBJECT on CAMEL_RIDER (player 1) [path "Defeat - Pack Camel Lost 3"]
issues_found: The caravan's pack animals are CAMEL_RIDER units (armed cavalry) when the engine ships TRADE_CART — and even the unarmed SHEEP/gaia options — which would represent laden pack beasts far better; an avoidable choice that turns a merchant train into a mounted squadron.

The Polo escort is composed of KNIGHT x2, CROSSBOWMAN x3 and MAN_AT_ARMS x3 — a Western European retinue of feudal heavy cavalry and crossbows that no Venetian merchant family took across the Pamirs; the Polos travelled with a handful of servants and local guides, not a knightly household.

Elevation is uniformly 0 across the entire 120x120 map, so the 'mountain passes of Central Asia' that the brief and the [D3] Mountain Pass trigger both name simply do not exist as terrain; the six CLIFF_DEFAULT_2 objects are decoration, not a pass or chokepoint.

The only water is a single ~3-tile patch at roughly one-third of the map's height, and the terrain is otherwise undifferentiated sand for 14,400 tiles — no Oxus crossing, no Wakhan corridor, no Gobi contrast, no visible route or road.

Marco Polo is represented by a KING unit, which will read to the player as a crowned monarch rather than a teenage Venetian merchant; a renamed generic (villager, or the same treatment given Niccolo) would have been less misleading, and pairing a KING with a VILLAGER_MALE father is internally inconsistent.

Shangdu, the destination the whole scenario turns on, is a GAIA cluster of one CASTLE, one TOWN_CENTER, three yurts and two guard towers — Kublai Khan himself is not present as any object, so the 'court of the great Khan' the narration promises is an empty set of neutral buildings.

The 'Bandit Chieftain' is attached to Mongol regular cavalry (CAVALRY_ARCHER x6, LIGHT_CAVALRY x4) while the text calls them 'Khaidu's horsemen' — Kaidu's forces were a rival Chagatai/Ogedeid army, not bandits, and conflating the two blurs a real political distinction the Polos' route actually turned on.
strengths: Player 1 as ITALIANS is exactly right for Venetian merchants and yields Mediterranean architecture for the caravan's tents and market; Player 2 as MONGOLS is right for the steppe raiders and yields yurts.

Every narrative beat is gated on BRING_OBJECT_TO_AREA rather than a timer, so the oasis, the ambush, the pass and the approach to Shangdu arrive in route order and only when the player advances the caravan.
The [D2] Bandit Ambush trigger fires ten PATROL effects on reaching an area, producing a genuine road ambush that emerges as the caravan passes rather than a scripted attack on a clock.
Victory is BRING_OBJECT_TO_AREA on Marco reaching the Shangdu corner of the map — the actual historical goal, arrival of the person at the place, not a battlefield kill.
Defeat conditions encode the real risks of the journey: the death of Marco, the death of Niccolo, or the loss of any of the three pack animals, so the trade goods matter as much as the men.
Dates are accurate throughout: departure in 1271, arrival at Shangdu in 1275, Niccolo as the returning veteran and Marco as the young newcomer.
justification: The scenario gets the frame right — Italians escorting a named Marco and Niccolo eastward to Mongol Shangdu, with victory turning on Marco's arrival and defeat on the loss of the men or the pack animals, all gated on the caravan's progress rather than a clock. It is undone by the map and the roster: elevation is flat 0 everywhere despite a [D3] Mountain Pass trigger and a brief built around mountain passes, and the 'pack camels' are armed CAMEL_RIDER cavalry escorted by knights, crossbowmen and men-at-arms when the engine's TRADE_CART was available and a merchant train needed no feudal retinue. Kublai Khan is absent from his own palace, which is a neutral CASTLE and TOWN_CENTER with three yurts.

justification: The scenario gets the frame right: Italians escorting a renamed King and villager to a Mongol-dressed Shangdu, with the correct 1271-1275 dating and a victory condition that is precisely the historical goal, chained through five spatially-gated waypoints. It fails on the two things it advertises most loudly: the elevation grid is uniformly zero, so the 'mountain passes of Central Asia' and the Pamir crossing exist only as dialogue and six cliff props on flat sand, and the 'pack camels' whose survival the mission hinges on are CAMEL_RIDER cavalry when TRADE_CART was available in the engine. Maffeo Polo's total absence and the recasting of the Mongol prince Kaidu as a desert bandit chieftain further blunt the portrait, though the narration itself asserts nothing false about the journey.

title: The Battle of Hastings
objective_facts:
EXTRACTED VICTORY AND DEFEAT CONDITIONS
(taken directly from the trigger graph; score `objective` from
these, not from the objectives text)

Victory:
  - DESTROY_OBJECT on KING (player 2) [path "VC - Harold Slain"]
Defeat:
  - DESTROY_OBJECT on WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR (player 1) [path "Defeat - William Slain"]
  - TIMER on 1500s elapsed [path "Defeat - Nightfall"]
issues_found: Elevation grid is entirely 0 across the whole 120x120 map: Senlac Hill, the single feature the battle turned on, does not exist. The narration repeatedly speaks of 'atop Senlac Hill' and luring the fyrd 'down the slope' over dead-flat ground.

A full-width water channel is cut across the map at roughly the one-third mark, separating the two halves. Hastings involved no river, strait or crossing; this is an invented obstacle that also contradicts the brief's open-field assault on a hilltop line.

Both armies are given Town Centers, Houses, a Monastery, a Barracks, Stable and Archery Range. Hastings was a single-day field engagement between two armies in the open; there was no settlement, and the Anglo-Saxon monastery (Battle Abbey) was founded only after the battle.
Player 2 is given 2 Archers; Anglo-Saxon archery at Hastings was famously almost nonexistent, and the Britons assignment additionally implies longbow access that is wrong for Harold's force.
All narration beats (William's rally, Harold's defiance, the feigned-retreat hint) are timer-gated, so the dialogue sequence plays out identically regardless of player action.
Defeat on the death of William is a counterfactual: William survived and had horses killed under him, but the rumour of his death was itself a turning point that goes unrepresented.
strengths: WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR, the engine's correct hero for this exact figure and battle, is used for Player 1 rather than a renamed generic.
Harold is represented by a renamed KING unit, the correct handling given the engine ships no Harold Godwinson hero.

Force composition is genuinely differentiated: Norman side is cavalry-and-archer heavy (10 Knights, 6 Light Cavalry, 8 Archers) while the Anglo-Saxon side is infantry-only in substance (6 Champions as housecarls, 14 Spearmen as fyrd), matching the sources' contrast.
Franks for the Normans (cavalry civilization, Western European architecture) and Britons for the Anglo-Saxons are apt period assignments.
The feigned-retreat turning point is gated on OBJECTS_IN_AREA rather than a timer, so the fyrd breaking ranks actually depends on the player performing the withdrawal.
Victory on slaying Harold and defeat on failing to break the wall by nightfall (1500s timer) are both the historically decisive conditions.
Narration is factually sound: 14 October 1066, Duke William's claim, the shield wall, the road to London, and Harold's death collapsing English resistance.
justification: The scenario casts the battle correctly - the actual William the Conqueror hero, a renamed King for Harold, and a differentiated Norman cavalry/archer force against an infantry shield wall - and encodes exactly the right win/lose pair (kill Harold, or fail before nightfall). Its fatal flaw is terrain: the elevation grid is uniformly zero, so Senlac Hill, the ridge the entire engagement was fought over, is absent, while a wholly invented river channel bisects the map. The result is text and triggers that talk about a hill and a slope on ground that is perfectly flat, plus Town Centers and a Monastery that belong to no part of a one-day field battle.

Harold is represented by a renamed KING unit — the correct handling, since AoE2 ships no Harold Godwinson hero.

Franks for the Normans (cavalry-centric, Western European architecture) and Britons for the Anglo-Saxons are the apt civilization proxies available.
Light Cavalry are supplied specifically to enact the feigned retreat, and the 'Fyrd Lured' trigger fires on units entering an area — a real mechanical representation of the fyrd breaking ranks.
Victory on Harold's death and defeat both on William's death and on a 1500-second nightfall deadline are exactly the historical win/loss conditions: Harold needed only to hold until dark.

The failure is geographic and total: the elevation grid is uniformly zero, so Senlac Hill — the ridge the entire battle was about — is absent, while an unexplained water band and 2,400 trees plus gold and stone mines make the field a generic random map. Events are largely timer-fired narration rather than causally chained, though the OBJECTS_IN_AREA 'Fyrd Lured' trigger is a genuine attempt to model the feigned retreat, and the surrounding Town Centers, Stable and Monastery misrepresent a one-day field engagement as a settled base battle.

The force composition is where it fails: the Turkish civilization's Janissary, the iconic infantry that stormed this gate, is entirely absent in favour of six camel riders, six cavalry archers and four light cavalry, while two bombard cannon supply the heavy artillery Suleiman notoriously did not have. The three assaults and the withdrawal are timer-gated in the right order but with a fabricated 29 September assault and Salm's wounding moved from 14 to 11 October.

title: The Siege of Vienna
objective_facts:
EXTRACTED VICTORY AND DEFEAT CONDITIONS
(taken directly from the trigger graph; score `objective` from
these, not from the objectives text)

Victory:
  - TIMER on 300s elapsed [path "VC - Siege Lifted"]

  - OBJECTS_IN_AREA on count 3, player 2, area (40,60)-(55,75) [path "Defeat - City Falls"]
issues_found: The garrison is built from CROSSBOWMAN x8 despite the narration explicitly naming 'Spanish arquebusiers' — the engine offers Hand Cannoneer, so gunpowder infantry was available and the substitution is avoidable.
The Ottoman roster contains no JANISSARY at all, even though the assigned Turks civilization supplies that exact unit and the janissary corps was the core of Suleiman's assault troops at Vienna.

Ottoman siege train is represented by MANGONEL x3 and ONAGER x2 (stone-throwing catapults) alongside only 2 bombard cannon; historically Suleiman had left his heavy guns behind and relied on light artillery and mining, so the catapult-heavy mix misrepresents the technology of 1529.
CAMEL_RIDER x6 and LIGHT_CAVALRY are placed in an assault role rather than as the akinci raiders who actually ranged the countryside; the besieging force reads as a generic Turkish army.

Suleiman is represented by a generic KING; acceptable as a renamed generic, but a Sultan commanding from a pavilion beside a bonfire with a single villager is thin for an army the sources put at over 100,000.

Nearly every turning point (first, second and third assaults, the rains, the withdrawal) fires on a bare TIMER, so the three dated assaults arrive identically regardless of player action; only the countermine has a genuine branch.

1,414 TREE_OAK tiles blanket the map; the ground before Vienna's Carinthian Gate was cleared glacis and suburb, not dense forest, and heavy woodland conceals the open approach the Ottomans actually had to cross.
Salm is said to be wounded on 11 October; his mortal wound came during the final assault of 14 October (he died the following May).
strengths: Both active players are correctly assigned: TEUTONS for the German/Austrian defenders and TURKS for the Ottomans, giving period-apt architecture for Vienna and the Ottoman camp.
The water band runs across the north of the map with the Ottoman camp and the walled city to the south, placing the Danube in the correct relation to the defences and the besiegers' start.
192 STONE_WALL tiles with a single named GATE_NORTH_TO_SOUTH reproduce the Carinthian Gate as the chokepoint the whole siege turned on, backed by KEEP and GUARD_TOWER.

The countermine sequence is genuinely interactive: DESTROY_OBJECT on the renamed sapper yields the 'mine defused' outcome, while BRING_OBJECT_TO_AREA yields a breach that spawns assault troops — the historically pivotal mining duel.
Victory is a TIMER (outlast the siege) and defeat is OBJECTS_IN_AREA for Ottoman troops reaching the city heart — exactly the asymmetric win/lose condition the defenders of Vienna faced.

Dated narration (29 September bombardment, 6 and 11 October assaults, mid-October rains, 14 October withdrawal) tracks the real chronology and gives the correct causes for the Ottoman retreat: mud, exhausted supplies and approaching winter.
justification: Civilizations, the walled chokepoint at the Carinthian Gate, the Danube to the north, and the timer-victory/breakthrough-defeat pair are all right for 1529, and the countermine is the one turning point the player can actually alter. The force composition, however, contradicts its own text: 'Spanish arquebusiers' are placed as CROSSBOWMAN when Hand Cannoneers exist in the engine, and the Turkish player fields camels, mangonels and onagers but not a single JANISSARY despite being assigned the very civilization that supplies them. The three assaults are all bare TIMER events, so the siege plays out identically whatever the garrison does, and 1,414 oaks forest over ground that was in fact cleared glacis.
